newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KURO APARATURA FAILS TO AGREE ON DIVIDENDS.
newsitem.headline: KURO APARATURA FAILS TO AGREE ON DIVIDENDS.

text.p: Lithuania's Kuro Aparatura general shareholders meeting failed to reach agreement over dividends but decided on a six million litas new share issue, company officials said on Monday.
"The general shareholders meeting on Saturday did not succeed to decide on dividends," finance director Dalia Zhilinskaite told Reuters.
"We had net profit of 16.2 million litas in 1996 and the shareholders could not decide how to share 15.7 million litas," Zhiliskaite added.

"The state representative wanted to pay in dividends 3.5 percent from the share capital of 43.2 million litas, the bigger investors wanted to keep the profit in the company and the board planned to pay 0.25 litas per share," Zhilinskaite said.
The state has a 32 percent stake in Kuro Aparatura.
"Now the decision will have to be taken in the shareholders meeting in June, Zhilinskaite said.
Zhilinskaite also said that a new six million litas share issue was agreed.
